prompt: Here's a `ChatService.accept()` handler from a realtime chat backend. Every accepted send is supposed to get a monotonic sequence number via Redis `INCR` and be appended to a per-room timeline via `ZADD`, while a `SET NX` dedup marker is meant to make redelivery of the same `messageId` a no-op. In practice, when a client retries a send with the exact same `messageId` (e.g. after a timeout on the first response), `seq:{roomId}` advances a second time and a duplicate-content row shows up in `log:{roomId}`. Walk me through the code and tell me exactly why that happens, name the invariant it violates, then give me the corrected version and a test that would catch this regression.
